edges.description: Reduced reductase activity impairs de novo dNTP synthesis.
Imbalanced and insufficient dNTPs impair mtDNA replication.
Stalled replication and faulty repair in post-mitotic muscle generate multiple mtDNA deletions.
Clonal expansion of deleted mtDNA produces mosaic respiratory-chain deficiency.
The mtDNA-deletion burden also involves the gastrointestinal tract in the MNGIE-like family.
Limb-muscle energy failure produces proximal weakness.
Muscle fibre damage releases creatine kinase.
Chronic myopathy produces limb muscle atrophy.
Respiratory-chain deficiency is seen as COX-negative fibres.
Mitochondrial proliferation is seen as ragged-red fibres.
Enteric involvement produces nausea and vomiting.
Gut dysmotility and malabsorption produce weight loss.
dNTP imbalance drives muscle mtDNA depletion, as inferred for the human disease.
edges.limitations: An overexpression/imbalance model, not the RRM1 R381 loss-of-function allele, and it produces depletion rather than the deletions seen in patient muscle.
